How Much Does Roof Cleaning Cost?

What three national publishers report for roof cleaning, the details that push a Houston roof toward the top or bottom of those ranges, and why the cheapest method can end up the most expensive.

Call (832) 662-4107 Send a Cleaning Request
  1. Home
  2. Guides
  3. Roof Cleaning Cost

Roof cleaning in Houston is priced on the roof itself: how big it is, how steep, how high, what it is made of and how much black growth is on it. The national figures below give a sense of scale. Your own roof cleaning Houston cost comes from a company that has looked at your roof.

This site and its phone number belong to a free referral line, not a roof cleaning business. It sets no prices and earns nothing from you. What follows is a plain guide to the published numbers and to the decisions that change them, so the price you are given makes sense when you hear it.

About these figures. The ranges come from HomeAdvisor, Forbes Home and This Old House and are national numbers those publishers put out themselves. They are not prices from this line or from the company it puts you through to, and that company names its own figure for your roof. They were checked in October 2026 as each publisher showed them at the time; follow the Sources links for any later updates.

Published roof cleaning cost ranges

National roof cleaning cost figures as published by HomeAdvisor, Forbes Home and This Old House, checked October 2026
PublisherTypical or average figureFull range shownPer square foot
HomeAdvisor (page labelled 2025 data)Average about $461; typical $296 to $625$150 to $1,000$0.50 to $1 to pressure or power wash a roof
Forbes HomeAverage $765 for a 1,700 sq ft roof$340 to $1,190 for that sizeSoft wash about $0.30 to $0.75

Notice that the three publishers describe the method differently. HomeAdvisor's page is titled around pressure cleaning, while Forbes Home and This Old House break out soft washing, the low-pressure method shingle makers point to. When you read any roof price, check which method it describes.

What shapes the price of a Houston roof

Every published range above moves with the same handful of details. The table shows which way each one usually pushes.

Roof details that affect cleaning cost and how each one tends to move the price
DetailToward the lower endToward the higher end
Roof sizeSmall, simple roof with few hips and valleysLarge roof with dormers, valleys and several levels. Roof area is bigger than the house footprint, and the steeper the roof, the bigger the gap.
PitchLow slope the crew can walkSteep slope that needs harnesses, roof anchors or a lift, and slower, more careful work
StoriesSingle storyTwo or three stories, longer ladders and more setup
MaterialAsphalt shingles in sound conditionConcrete or clay tile that can crack underfoot, or metal panels with coating and warranty rules
How heavy the growth isLight streaking from algaeThick black streaks, moss or lichen that need more solution and more time
AccessOpen driveway side, easy ladder footingPool, fragile landscaping or a fence right under the eaves
Tree coverFull sun most of the dayOverhanging oaks or pines that shade the roof and drop debris

Shingles, tile and metal are priced differently

Asphalt shingles are the most common Houston roof and the one the published ranges mostly describe. The black streaks are algae, mainly Gloeocapsa magma, which is often mistaken for soot or dirt. The manufacturers' guidance is consistent: a gentle cleaning solution and a low-pressure rinse, without scrubbing. You can read more on the roof cleaning service page.

Concrete and clay tile takes more care. Eagle Roofing, a concrete tile maker, warns that walking on wet tile is dangerous, that tiles can break, and that some cleaning products can affect or etch the surface, and it recommends an experienced, insured professional. Slower work and replacement of any cracked tiles both feed into the price.

Metal roofs often clean up with less effort, but Metal Sales advises checking the panel maker's cleaning guidance and warranty first, because some warranties name the cleaners and methods allowed. A careful company asks what panels you have before it quotes.

Why the cheapest roof price can cost the most

The fastest way to clean a roof is to blast it. It is also the way the industry's own manufacturers say not to do it.

  • ARMA: the Asphalt Roofing Manufacturers Association's bulletin rules out high-pressure systems on asphalt roofs as likely to cause damage, and it advises against scrubbing because friction loosens granules.
  • GAF: its technical bulletin on algae staining recommends a cleaning solution rinsed at low pressure and cautions that power washing can knock granules loose, which cuts years off a shingle roof.
  • Owens Corning: its guidance is not to scrub or use high-pressure power washing, because removing granules shortens the life of the roof.

Those granules shield the asphalt from Texas sun. A roof that loses them early ages early, and a replacement costs far more than any cleaning. So a lower quote built on high pressure is not a saving. When two roof quotes differ widely, ask each company how it will clean the roof and judge them on that answer first.

Making a roof price add up over time

Angi's published rule of thumb is a cleaning every one to three years, leaning toward the short end in damp, shady places. A few habits stretch the gap between cleanings, which matters more over the life of a roof than shaving a little off one bill.

  • Trim back overhanging branches. Purdue Extension notes mildew grows most where trees and shrubs restrict air movement. More sun and air mean a drier roof.
  • Ask about zinc strips. ARMA says zinc strips near the ridge may reduce regrowth of algae and moss, as rain carries metal ions down the slope.
  • Plan for algae-resistant shingles at replacement. Owens Corning and CertainTeed both make shingles with copper-bearing granules that inhibit growth.
  • Pair it with the gutters. If the company is already set up at the eaves, ask what it would charge to brighten the gutter faces too. See gutter cleaning and brightening.

Questions that tell you a roof price is sound

  1. "Is this priced on roof area or the house's square footage?" They are different numbers, and roof area is the honest one.
  2. "Will you soft wash, and will anyone scrub or use high pressure on the shingles?" You want a yes and a no.
  3. "How will you protect the plants, gutters and anything under the eaves?" Runoff from a roof lands on beds, pool decks and patio furniture.
  4. "Can I see your liability insurance certificate?" Roof work happens at height, and a slip or a cracked tile needs someone to pay for it.

For the general version of these questions, see how to get a pressure washing quote. For ground-level surfaces like the driveway and siding, how much pressure washing costs has the published figures.

Common questions

Is it cheaper to pressure wash a roof than soft wash it?

It may look cheaper on paper, but the shingle industry's trade group, ARMA, tells homeowners to keep high-pressure systems off asphalt roofs altogether because of the damage they tend to cause, and GAF and Owens Corning both warn that it knocks loose the granules that protect shingles. Losing granules shortens a roof's life, so the saving can disappear quickly. Ask any company which method it plans to use before comparing prices.

How often does a roof need cleaning in Houston?

Angi's guidance puts the usual gap at one to three years, shorter where the air is humid and trees hang over the roof. Houston fits both descriptions on many streets, so a shaded north slope may need attention sooner than a sunny one on the same house.

Does cleaning my roof void the shingle warranty?

Not automatically, but read your warranty. Shingle makers warn that high-pressure washing strips granules, and damage caused by the wrong cleaning method may not be covered. Some metal panel makers also specify which cleaners and methods their warranty allows. A soft wash that follows the maker's guidance is the safer route.

Will the black streaks come back after the roof is cleaned?

They can, because the algae behind them, mainly Gloeocapsa magma, spreads through the air. ARMA says zinc strips near the ridge may slow regrowth, and algae-resistant shingles with copper granules are an option when a roof is replaced. Trimming branches that shade the roof also helps it dry faster.

Can I get a roof cleaning price over the phone?

A company may give a rough figure from your roof size, pitch and photos, but expect it to want a look before it commits, since growth and access are hard to judge from the street. Calling (832) 662-4107 is free, and the company you are put through to sets its own price.
